Scan. Classify. Recycle Right.

Contamination and human sorting error cost the global recycling industry billions every year — and send millions of tons of recoverable material to landfill instead. RecycLens pairs computer vision with embedded hardware to classify waste in real time: the technical foundation for automated sorting systems built to hold accuracy at the scale a recycling facility actually runs at.

How It Works

Three steps to a cleaner bin

01

Take or upload a photo

Snap a picture with your device camera or drag in an existing image.

02

AI analyzes the image

A CNN model processes the image and identifies the material in milliseconds.

03

Get instant guidance

See the category, confidence score, and exactly how to dispose of it.

Powered by a TensorFlow CNN trained on 15 waste categories, served via a FastAPI backend.

Waste Categories

15 categories, one bin at a time

RecycLens recognizes the full range of common household and e-waste materials.

15categories
  • Recyclable8 · 53%
  • Special Disposal6 · 40%
  • Landfill1 · 7%

Recyclable

8

  • Cardboard

    Flatten boxes and keep dry before placing in the recycling bin.

  • Glass

    Rinse clean and remove lids before recycling.

  • Metal

    Rinse cans and crush if possible to save space.

  • Paper

    Keep dry and free of food residue before recycling.

  • Plastic

    Check the resin code and rinse before placing in the bin.

  • White Glass

    Clear glass goes in its own stream — rinse before recycling.

  • Brown Glass

    Sort separately from clear and green glass, then rinse.

  • Green Glass

    Sort separately from clear and brown glass, then rinse.

Special Disposal

6

  • Battery

    Never bin loose — drop off at a battery collection point.

  • Clothes

    Donate if wearable, otherwise use a textile recycling bin.

  • Shoes

    Pair up and donate, or drop off at a shoe recycling point.

  • Biological

    Compost food and garden waste where a composting bin is available.

  • E-Waste

    Take to a certified e-waste facility — never bin electronics.

  • Medical

    Requires biohazard disposal — return to a pharmacy or clinic.

Landfill

1

  • Trash

    Not recoverable — dispose of in general landfill waste.

The Bigger Picture

Built to grow into hardware

This scanner is the computer-vision core of something bigger: an AI-powered sorting system that runs on physical hardware, mounted above a conveyor belt, classifying and diverting waste in real time at the scale a recycling facility actually runs at.

Recycling facilities lose billions annually to sorting errors and contamination. We're building an AI-powered sorting system that runs on commodity edge hardware — aiming to replace $500K optical sorters with a sub-$2K solution.

Our mission

In progress

Building the prototype

  • Jetson Nano + camera running a TensorRT-optimized model
  • Small conveyor belt mock-up
  • Servo-actuated diverter triggered by the classification output
  • Real-time accuracy and throughput metrics
In progress

Strengthening the model

  • Filming real sorting scenarios to build a better training dataset
  • Testing against material types the current model handles poorly
  • Documenting power draw, inference speed, and error rates
Ongoing

Talking to facilities

  • Reaching out to local recycling facilities to offer live demos
  • One facility saying “we’d pay for this” outweighs any pitch deck
